module-guide.text:
Game controller

Owns the only frame loop, input dispatch, camera, and Play/Edit state. Waits for physics and rendering before starting the next frame.
Shared state is on Stage. Cross-sprite requests use broadcast and wait; do not start another frame loop.

interface-guide.text:
Requests received

detach rider
edit track
home view
play or pause
retry
select edit mode
select play mode
step once
toggle full play

module-guide.text:
Physics

Rider, sled, collisions, spatial grid and cached timeline frames. Solver iterations and snapshot writes are local custom-block calls.
Shared state is on Stage. Cross-sprite requests use broadcast and wait; do not start another frame loop.

module-guide.text:
Renderer

The only sprite that clears or draws the shared pen layer. Draws terrain/rider, then chrome, then overlays. All costumes and glyphs live here.
Shared state is on Stage. Cross-sprite requests use broadcast and wait; do not start another frame loop.

prompt-history-index.text:
Prompt history

27 user prompts in order. Public usernames are kept; passwords, private contact details and local paths are redacted. Automatic context is omitted.

prompt-01.text:
Prompt 01

Using the MCP server in "[local path]", find out if Ricky-Jan's Force2D package would be suitable for this project. I want to recreate Line Rider in Scratch. I think this is a good idea for a game to recreate in Scratch because it has relatively simple rigid physics and is fun. We need to find the best Rigid Body physics engine for this in Scratch. It should be performant, have good enough collisions so that there can be one body held inside of another body but can be flung out (the player and the sled respectively), have good support for lines that are drawn with varying friction levels. The lines are very important, because if it treats each segment as a rectangle then it would not look smooth and the player would jump and stuff. It should support scrolling. Work on this.
